source.name: Form fields inside a disabled fieldset must not be treated as tabbable, so a focus-trapped dialog focuses its first usable field
source.scope: Real upstream bug (https://github.com/focus-trap/tabbable/issues/413) at cc8b7b2bc4319b672d0e6053b34c732168dd035c. Blind to the maintainers' fix 1d5fcb51d9eb21994c82a2f03010bc0d017cfff2; routing auto.

journey.title: Opening the address dialog puts focus on the first usable field
journey.goal: A keyboard user can open the dialog, type an address and save it

functionalJourney.title: Save the address dialog with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: The dialog opens, saves and closes

success.value: Delivery address saved without a street.

functional.value: Delivery address saved without a street.

guards.title: Escape closes the address dialog and returns focus
guards.goal: Escape dismisses the dialog and focus returns to the trigger

plan.root_cause: The focus trap's default delayInitialFocus option defers setting initial focus to the next tick, leaving focus on the triggering button when the test asserts focus immediately after opening the dialog.
plan.repair_strategy: Disable delayInitialFocus in the focus trap configuration so initial focus is applied synchronously upon activation.

edits.before: const trap = createFocusTrap('#address-dialog', { onDeactivate: () => { backdrop.hidden = true; } });
edits.after: const trap = createFocusTrap('#address-dialog', { onDeactivate: () => { backdrop.hidden = true; }, delayInitialFocus: false });

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users will receive immediate focus on the first usable field (street input) when the address dialog opens, satisfying focus order expectations.
functional_risks: Altering delayInitialFocus may affect edge cases where external code expects a delayed focus, but the trap is used solely for this dialog.
verification_requirements: After activating the dialog, focus must be on #street.
Pressing Tab should move focus sequentially through #street, #save, #cancel, then wrap.
Pressing Escape must close the dialog and return focus to the #open button.
Saving an address with or without a street must update the status correctly.

plan.root_cause: The focus trap's default delayInitialFocus: true defers initial focus to the next event loop tick, causing the test's immediate focus assertion to fail. Additionally, the tabbable detection may not reliably select the street input as the first focusable element due to the disabled fieldset and dynamic visibility.
plan.repair_strategy: Explicitly configure the focus trap with initialFocus: '#street' to guarantee the correct element receives focus, and set delayInitialFocus: false to apply focus synchronously during activation.

edits.before: const trap = createFocusTrap('#address-dialog', { onDeactivate: () => { backdrop.hidden = true; } });
edits.after: const trap = createFocusTrap('#address-dialog', { onDeactivate: () => { backdrop.hidden = true; }, initialFocus: '#street', delayInitialFocus: false });

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users will receive immediate focus on the street input when the address dialog opens, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 and 2.4.3 focus order requirements.
functional_risks: If the street input is removed or hidden in future changes, the explicit initialFocus selector will throw an error; however, the current structure is stable.
Setting delayInitialFocus to false may affect edge cases where external code expects a delayed focus, but the trap is used solely for this dialog.
verification_requirements: After activating the dialog via Enter on #open, focus must be on #street.
Pressing Tab should move focus sequentially through #street, #save, #cancel, then wrap.
Pressing Escape must close the dialog and return focus to the #open button.
Saving an address with or without a street must update the status correctly.
